purpose: Acting references; exported faces preserve existing native-pixel identity.
toby:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create a production acting reference sprite sheet derived strictly from the supplied Victorian point-and-click portrait. Same character identity, hair, age, head proportions, costume, 3/4 right-facing viewpoint and warm limited ochre palette in EVERY panel. Crisp coarse pixel clusters appropriate to a 56x64 face, no smooth painting, no cartoon squash, no new lighting. Remove the gold frame for this reference sheet only. Uniform flat dark aubergine backdrop. Arrange NINE equally sized busts in a precise 3-column by 3-row grid; each bust has identical scale and head position. Small labels below each panel. The top six panels are expression keys, the bottom three are coherent whole-bust gesture keys (natural connected shoulder/upper arm/elbow/wrist anatomy; NEVER a detached hand). These are reference drawings to inform native pixel edits; do not invent extra props.
Top row left to right: neutral anxious (copy reference), frightened (inner eyebrows raised, eyes wider, tight trembling lips), tearful (reddened lids, one visible tear, distressed inner brows). Second row: spooked (eyes glance aside, tense lips), earnest (brows raised, attentive), relieved (soft eyes, slight closed smile). Bottom row: cap habit start with both hands holding a brown cloth flat cap low against chest; middle both hands twist the cap slightly inward; end hands relax cap. Keep the young man's ungloved hands small, sleeves visibly connected; his head and face unchanged during habit.
